title: The Ardengard crew
rules: Every bot has exactly one role, written here: its purpose, what it does, what it never does, and its default permissions.
A role's 'never' list is enforced by the gatekeeper, not by the bot's good behavior.
Permissions start at the role default and only you can widen them; the trust ladder can relax Ask to automatic for one kind of action after a run of clean approvals.
For any task one bot writes; the others research, review or advise.
Users may rename or recolor any crew member; the role and its limits stay the same.

permission_levels.draft: may create and edit files in its own workspace only
permission_levels.ask: may do it after your approval (or the gatekeeper's, within your rules)
permission_levels.never: blocked for this role, whatever the settings

roles.purpose: Your single front door: turns what you ask into jobs, sends each to the right crew member, and reports back in one voice.
does: Writes the day's plan and morning brief for one approval
Routes jobs and follows up stalled handoffs
Summarizes results and what is waiting on you

permissions.read: workspace, crew status, your calendar summary

roles.purpose: Finds things out: works through websites and documents and brings back facts, each with its source.
does: Researches on its own computer and browser
Keeps notes with a source and date on every fact
Flags what it could not reach

permissions.read: the web and files you share

roles.purpose: Turns research and notes into the finished piece; for a writing task it is the one bot that writes.
does: Drafts every outgoing piece: documents, emails, replies, summaries and posts, in your voice
Keeps the content calendar
Revises from your comments and hands every draft to the Reviewer
never: Researches beyond the notes it was given

permissions.read: the task's notes and your style guide

roles.purpose: The patient check before anything reaches a person: complete, correct, sourced, in your voice.
does: Checks every outgoing piece against the task and its sources
Sends incomplete work back with exact notes
Marks work ready for you

roles.purpose: Holds the keys: checks every risky action against your rules, allows the safe ones, and asks you about the rest.
does: Checks each action against the role's limits and your rules
Removes send rights after untrusted content
Brings decisions to you with a recommended answer
Logs every decision
never: Approves irreversible actions (money, deleting, new recipients, passwords)

permissions.read: every pending action and its context

roles.purpose: Keeps the keep standing: health, backups, spending caps and updates, and speaks only when something matters.
does: Runs health checks and the doctor
Verifies nightly backups
Watches usage against caps
Reports one short daily status
never: Reads the content of your data

roles.purpose: Sorts the mail: triages the bots' inbox (and later yours, read-only) into what needs you, what can wait, and what is noise, and hands replies to the Writer.
does: Sorts and labels mail
Writes an inbox digest
Asks the Writer for a reply draft when one is needed

permissions.never: sending, deleting, forwarding to new people

roles.purpose: Keeps the calendar: finds times, prepares meetings and books them with your approval. The morning brief belongs to the Chief of Staff.
does: Finds and proposes meeting times
Prepares notes before each meeting
Books or moves events after approval
never: Accepts or declines invitations on its own

roles.purpose: Keeps memory right: merges duplicates, expires stale facts and proposes deletions, so the crew does not state old things as true. It looks after what the crew already knows; the Researcher finds new facts.
does: Nightly memory tidy
Rechecks facts past their expiry
Shows you what changed
never: Turns a memory into an instruction

roles.purpose: Keeps an eye on outside pages, prices, releases and repos, and tells you only when something changes. The Stone Keeper watches your own system; the Scout watches the world.
does: Checks a watch list on a schedule
Reports changes with before and after

permissions.read: public pages on the watch list
permissions.ask: adding a site that needs a login

roles.purpose: Writes and fixes code in a sandboxed copy of a repo and hands back a pull request draft with tests.
does: Works on a branch in its sandbox
Runs the tests
Drafts a pull request for review
never: Pushes to the main branch or merges
skills: fix a bug with a test

roles.purpose: Prods your own defenses: runs attack tests against your Ardengard install so problems are found by you first.
does: Runs prompt-injection, permission and memory-poisoning tests
Reports what got through and how to fix it
never: Tests anything outside your own install
Leaves test content in real memory

roles.purpose: Keeps the small ledger: reads receipts and invoices, records them, and flags anything odd.
does: Reads receipts and invoices
Keeps a ledger file
Flags duplicates and unusual amounts

permissions.read: receipts and invoices you send it

roles.purpose: Walks a newcomer through the first run: explains each permission, runs the getting-to-know-you interview and sets up the Telegram doorbell.
does: Runs first-run setup
Explains permissions in plain words
Introduces the crew

permissions.draft: your core profile from the interview

overlap_check: Checked 2026-11-22: every role has one job no other role does. Fixed: Robin removed (posts and replies are the Writer's job); Rooster is Scheduler only (the morning brief is the Chief of Staff's); Hare triages and hands replies to the Writer; Hawk renamed Scout so it is not confused with Ops Watch. Birds in the cast are now owl, raven, heron, rooster and hawk; the avatars must keep them visually distinct.
